newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Yellow River water level at record low.
newsitem.headline: China's Yellow River water level at record low.

text.p: Water levels on China's Yellow River are the lowest in decades due to several years of drought on the waterway's upper reaches, the Xinhua Daily Telegraph said on Sunday.

Six years of drought on the southwestern Qinghai-Tibetan plateau that feed the Yellow River about 75 percent of its water had reduced the flow in the river's upper reaches by more than one-quarter, the newspaper said.

The flow of water into the Longyang Gorge Reservoir that is used to monitor the river's water level had dropped by 33 cubic metres a second in the last three months to reach the lowest level in history, it said but gave no further details.
The Yellow River, China's second longest, cuts across its northern plains to Shandong province to the Bohai Sea.
